<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line" lang="en">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_align_center">Binhui Xie<sup id="id1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup>, Jinmin Li<sup id="id1.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup>, Haomiao Tang<sup id="id1.3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗</span></sup>, Guangting Wang<sup id="id1.4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">∗†</span></sup></span>
<br class="ltx_break">
<span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_align_center">
Song Jin, Jianwei Zhu, Fengyun Rao<sup id="id2.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">‡</span></sup>, Jing LYU
</span>
<br class="ltx_break">

<span id="id3" class="ltx_text ltx_align_center">WeChat Vision, Tencent Inc.
</span>
</span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five public) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks. On the e-commerce suite, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B surpasses substantially larger open-source flagship models, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. On the general-purpose suite, every WeMM-Ecom model surpasses its similarly sized Qwen3.5 counterpart, with the lightweight variants (e.g., WeMM-Ecom-2B) showing clear advantages over leading lightweight models such as Qwen3.5-2B, MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B, and LFM3-VL-2B. Beyond benchmarks, WeMM-Ecom now powers hundreds of production use cases in WeChat, including catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce, serving billion-scale requests per day. We publicly release all model weights and detail our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction to facilitate future work on domain-specialized multimodal models.</p>
    
<p id="abstract1.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><a href="https://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/wemm-ecom" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_align_left ltx_inline-block" style="width:14.8pt;position:relative; bottom:-1.8pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.30662v1/hf-icon.svg" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:14/13;" width="14" height="13"></object></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/wemm-ecom</span></a></p>
    
<p id="abstract1.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><a href="https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Ecom" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_align_left ltx_inline-block" style="width:14.8pt;position:relative; bottom:-1.8pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.30662v1/github-icon.svg" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:13/13;" width="13" height="13"></object></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Ecom</span></a></p>
  
</div>

  <sup id="footnotex1.2.2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="footnotex1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">‡</span></sup>Corresponding author: <a href="mailto:fengyunrao@tencent.com" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href"><span class="ltx_ref ltx_nolink">fengyunrao@tencent.com</span></a>
</span></span></span></span>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become capable general-purpose models for understanding images, documents, and video <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib79" title="" class="ltx_ref">79</a>, <a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>, <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>, <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>, <a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">86</a>, <a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">78</a>]</cite>. In specialized domains, however, general capability alone falls short, as models must apply fine-grained domain knowledge to what they see, whether identifying a clinical finding in a medical scan <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">72</a>]</cite> or extracting the correct figure from a financial chart <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">E-commerce is an especially demanding domain for MLLMs. A product can be presented through dozens of product views, long-form detail images, and livestream frames, alongside titles and structured attribute tables. Critical evidence, such as selling points, nutrition facts, dimension annotations, and certification marks, often appears only inside images. Models must further link this visual text to the specific SKU variant in question and draw on catalog knowledge that is never explicitly stated. As e-commerce models move from text records <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>, <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>, <a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite> to multimodal understanding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib91" title="" class="ltx_ref">91</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, two core challenges stand out: (1) models must accurately perceive dense, interleaved visual evidence and produce outputs that satisfy strict entity-level and business-rule constraints; and (2) domain specialization must not erode general visual perception and reasoning, especially for lightweight models deployed under tight latency and memory budgets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">99</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To address these challenges, we present <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WeMM-Ecom</span>, a family of multimodal foundation models spanning four dense sizes (0.8B, 2B, 4B, and 9B) and a 35B mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 3B active parameters (35B-A3B), initialized from Qwen3.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>]</cite>. We curate over 40 e-commerce tasks from product images, livestream frames, and business workflows. Because these tasks directly exercise visual grounding, OCR, and multi-image reasoning, they also strengthen general perception rather than competing with it. We pair them with broad general supervision in a two-stage continued pre-training (CPT) curriculum with an increased e-commerce share in the second stage (Figure <a href="#S2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Post-training then applies hybrid-thinking on-policy distillation (OPD), a single parameter-space merge with the post-trained Qwen3.5 weights that recovers general instruction-following and reasoning abilities, and group relative policy optimization (GRPO), enabling each model to support both thinking and non-thinking modes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate WeMM-Ecom on a comprehensive 28-benchmark e-commerce suite across eight scenarios (207,117 instances) and 64 general benchmarks. Across all five sizes and both modes, WeMM-Ecom consistently outperforms size-matched Qwen3.5 on e-commerce. WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B ranks first among evaluated flagships (Figure <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), surpassing Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, HY4, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017. In non-thinking mode, our 0.8B and 2B models each beat a larger Qwen3.5 model on e-commerce while showing clear advantages on general-purpose capabilities. WeMM-Ecom-2B also surpasses MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">99</a>]</cite> and LFM3-VL-2B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite> on both e-commerce and general suites in both thinking and non-thinking modes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Our main contributions are as follows:</p>
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">We open-source WeMM-Ecom</span>, a family of five multimodal models ranging from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B-A3B MoE model, each supporting both thinking and non-thinking modes. WeMM-Ecom delivers leading e-commerce performance at every scale while matching or surpassing its Qwen3.5 counterpart on general benchmarks, and has been validated at scale in production.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">We present a detailed training and data recipe for WeMM-Ecom</span>. We describe how more than 40 e-commerce tasks are constructed from product images, livestream frames, and business records; how they are mixed with general data and scheduled across two CPT stages; and how hybrid-thinking OPD, a one-time parameter-space merge, and GRPO are combined to produce the final models.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">We introduce the key design principles of our e-commerce evaluation framework</span>. We show how real-world business workflows are translated into eight evaluation scenarios with explicit inputs, decision targets, and scoring rules, resulting in a suite of 23 in-house and five public benchmarks with 207,117 instances.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Training</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We initialize each WeMM-Ecom model from the corresponding Qwen3.5 Base checkpoint <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>]</cite> and perform full-parameter optimization across all training stages using the WeChat-YATT framework <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">90</a>]</cite>. Our pipeline first conducts CPT to instill fine-grained knowledge of products, variants, and business rules while preserving broad multimodal capabilities. Subsequently, post-training combines OPD for token-level teacher guidance, a single parameter-space merge with the post-trained Qwen3.5 weights, and reinforcement learning (RL) driven by task-specific verifiable rewards. All five model scales support thinking and non-thinking modes in a unified chat interface. Figure <a href="#S2.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarizes the training and evaluation pipeline.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.30662v1/training_pipeline.svg" id="S2.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/113;" width="476" height="113"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S2.F2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Training and evaluation pipeline.<span id="S2.F2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> The e-commerce share increases in the second continued pre-training stage. Post-training combines on-policy distillation (OPD), checkpoint merging, and group relative policy optimization (GRPO). The resulting checkpoints support thinking and non-thinking modes and are evaluated on e-commerce and general benchmarks.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce</h3>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S2.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S2.F3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Token composition of the two CPT stages.<span id="S2.F3.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Inner sectors and adjacent bars show shares across five e-commerce and seven general domains; outer rings show proportion of general and e-commerce data. E-commerce accounts for 45.8% of 370.32B tokens in Stage 1 and 61.1% of 76.66B tokens in Stage 2. Domains are ranked independently within each group and stage, thus number indices are stage- and group-specific.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>

<td id="S2.T1.8.13.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-top:0.7pt;padding-bottom:0.7pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.13.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:238.1pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.13.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S2.T1.8.13.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Mathematics, science, and technical problems that require visual context
(diagrams, charts, documents, educational material, or video), with worked
solutions; includes chart-to-code tasks.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S2.T1.8.14" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T1.8.14.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-top:0.7pt;padding-bottom:0.7pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.14.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:93.2pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.14.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S2.T1.8.14.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Multimodal World Knowledge</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="S2.T1.8.14.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-top:0.7pt;padding-bottom:0.7pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.14.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:238.1pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.14.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S2.T1.8.14.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Linking visual entities and scenes to external facts: encyclopedia- and
entity-grounded image descriptions, knowledge-intensive VQA, and
specialized-domain tasks such as medical imaging.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S2.T1.8.15" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S2.T1.8.15.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.7pt;padding-bottom:0.7pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.15.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:93.2pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.15.1.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S2.T1.8.15.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Pure Text</span></span>
</span></td>
<td id="S2.T1.8.15.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-top:0.7pt;padding-bottom:0.7pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.15.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:238.1pt;">
<span id="S2.T1.8.15.2.1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><span id="S2.T1.8.15.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">General text-only records: mathematical and scientific reasoning,
instruction-following and multilingual dialogue, encyclopedic and
reading-comprehension text, and curated web text.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CPT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> adapts the backbone to e-commerce while preserving its general multimodal capabilities. We construct CPT data from product images, livestream frames, business records, and general multimodal and text-only corpora, and organize it into five e-commerce and seven general domains (Figure <a href="#S2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>; Table <a href="#S2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). We retain both pools throughout CPT because e-commerce tasks routinely depend on general skills: reading a package label and assigning it to the requested product, for example, draws on general OCR and grounding as well as knowledge of product variants. Records with an e-commerce business context, including text-only records, are assigned to the corresponding e-commerce domain.
Training proceeds in two stages; the second raises the e-commerce share and shifts emphasis from perception toward auditing and reasoning (Section <a href="#S2.SS1.SSS4" title="2.1.4 CPT Recipe ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.1.1 </span>E-Commerce Data</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">General multimodal corpora teach a model to recognize a bag of coffee beans;
e-commerce applications must also determine which variant it is—the 250 g
or the 500 g SKU, a single bag or a two-pack—whether its listing complies
with platform rules, and how to present it to shoppers. We therefore design
e-commerce supervision around three properties that general corpora rarely
provide: <span id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">variant-level granularity</span>, <span id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">traceable evidence</span>, and <span id="S2.SS1.SSS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">rule-conditioned
outputs</span>. The five domains in Table <a href="#S2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> instantiate these
properties in different combinations.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Variant-level granularity.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Product Perception &amp; Understanding trains the model to resolve products at the
level of categories, attributes, and SKUs. Category prediction pairs product
images with taxonomy labels and reasoning traces, and attribute tasks extract
visible text, properties, and regions from gallery images, detail strips, and
livestream frames. SKU attribute examples specify a variant and an attribute,
supply the relevant views and fields, and use the recorded value as the target;
a net-weight question, for instance, must distinguish the 250 g SKU from the
500 g SKU. Product Retrieval applies the same granularity to matching. Each
example pairs two listings, SKU records, or product regions with their
available images and specifications, and defines equivalence at the requested
level: a single 500 g bag and a two-pack of 250 g bags may depict the same
product and contain the same total quantity, yet their pack configurations make
them distinct SKUs. Region-level and cross-image examples extend matching to
comparisons between specified visual entities.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Traceable evidence.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We tie targets to the evidence that supports them so that outputs can be
checked against the source listing. SKU attribute examples retain the index of
the source image that contains the recorded value. Bounding-box annotations
localize products, brand logos, certification marks, specification tables, and
dimension annotations, and explicitly mark targets that are absent from the
image. In General E-Commerce Knowledge &amp; QA, listing images, descriptions,
visible text, and structured fields are paired with questions on product
knowledge, commerce OCR, and reasoning, with reference answers supported by the
supplied sources. Product descriptions, entity annotations, and articles
further connect product appearance with names, brands, uses, and business
knowledge.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Rule-conditioned outputs.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Many e-commerce decisions are defined by platform rules rather than by visual
content alone. Product Information Audit pairs listing titles, gallery images,
and attribute fields with platform governance rules and annotated compliance
decisions. Its tasks include identifying restricted goods, detecting
image–title or category inconsistencies, reviewing product-image quality, and
screening content for policy violations; each target specifies the applicable
rule and the decision, together with visual or textual evidence for tasks that
require an explanation. The same domain also covers quality review of short
product titles, where the target is a set of pass/fail judgments rather than a
rewritten title. E-Commerce Content Generation applies rules to generation
rather than judgment: short-title examples map structured product
specifications to concise, formatted titles that follow platform style
guidelines.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.1.2 </span>General-Purpose Data</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The seven general domains preserve the perception, language, knowledge, and
reasoning capabilities that e-commerce tasks build on and that the model needs
beyond them. They draw on curated sources and task mixtures, including all 162
nonempty sources in OpenBee <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib107" title="" class="ltx_ref">107</a>]</cite>. We summarize the main sources
below and describe shared construction procedures in
Section <a href="#S2.SS1.SSS3" title="2.1.3 Data Construction and Quality Control ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Perception and reading.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Multimodal Understanding pairs images with Chinese or English captions and adds
video data for event understanding and temporally grounded tasks, including
sports event narration and general video question answering. OCR, Documents,
and Charts pairs natural images, documents, charts, and tables with
transcriptions, reading questions, or structured extraction targets, covering
both the recognition of visible text and its use in document and chart
understanding; sources include ChartNet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>,
multilingual OCR collections, web articles, and table annotations.
Grounding and Detection converts object and region annotations from
Objects365 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">73</a>]</cite>, SA-1B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>, and
LocateAnything <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib85" title="" class="ltx_ref">85</a>]</cite> into localization and detection
targets conditioned on object names or referring descriptions, while GUI
examples associate interface instructions with the locations of the
corresponding elements.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reasoning and knowledge.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual Instruction &amp; Reasoning combines single-image QA, multi-image
comparison, visual quality assessment, and instruction-driven tasks. Each
example pairs the available views with a question or constrained instruction
and a reference answer, comparison judgment, or decision; multi-image questions
require integrating evidence across views, and edit-instruction examples ask
the model to infer, from a source image and its edited version, the
instruction that produced the change. Risk assessment and content moderation
tasks apply written platform policies to general content such as short videos;
unlike Product Information Audit, they do not review product listings.
Multimodal STEM pairs diagram- and video-based problems in mathematics,
science, and technical reasoning with worked solutions, including material from
Innovator-VL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib89" title="" class="ltx_ref">89</a>]</cite>, and adds chart and document problems
from educational corpora across biology, chemistry, mathematics, and K-12
science. Multimodal World Knowledge associates images with encyclopedic and
entity-specific descriptions from online wikis and entity recaption sources, and pairs
visual evidence with specialized questions whose answers draw on knowledge
beyond the visible appearance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Text-only data.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS2.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Pure Text retains general records without visual inputs as language and
instruction supervision. Mathematical and scientific reasoning dominate this
mixture, drawing on Nemotron-Math <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite> and Chinese STEM
sources, while instruction-following and multilingual dialogues, Wikipedia
text, reading-comprehension QA, and curated web text supply general language,
factual knowledge, and instruction-following supervision.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.1.3 </span>Data Construction and Quality Control</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several construction and filtering procedures are shared across domains.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Spatial targets and absent objects.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Conversion of box annotations in both pools makes coordinate normalization
explicit, preserves the source category schemas, and keeps each target linked
to its annotated visual entity. Both pools also encode absence explicitly:
e-commerce annotations mark targets missing from the image, and general
grounding data includes rejection examples whose queries name objects absent
from the image, teaching the model to decline rather than hallucinate a box.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Recaptioning.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We cluster images with WeMM-Embedding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib109" title="" class="ltx_ref">109</a>]</cite>, sample across
clusters for recaptioning, and deduplicate the resulting captions. For
text-rich images, PaddleOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite> transcriptions provide
textual cues for caption generation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Synthesized reasoning.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For synthesized STEM solutions, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B generates the reasoning and
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B checks answer agreement; malformed or truncated solutions are
discarded.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Web article mining.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two classifiers identify product-recommendation articles and select
comparative reviews or detailed accounts of product use. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B then
filters promotional or irrelevant material and extracts product and brand
facts, which we deduplicate with MinHash.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Source balancing.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS3.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When aggregating multi-source collections, we assign a token budget to each
source group and, where a group exceeds its budget, downsample its constituent
sources in proportion to their token counts, so that every source remains
represented.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.1.4 </span>CPT Recipe</h4>

<section id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Progressive data mixture.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adopt a two-stage curriculum that increases domain specialization while
maintaining broad general supervision (Figure <a href="#S2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Stage 1 establishes multimodal and
product representations with a 45.8% e-commerce share, and Stage 2 raises
the share to 61.1%. Within the e-commerce pool (percentages are shares within
each pool), supervision shifts from basic perception toward compliance auditing
and knowledge-intensive QA: Product Information Audit rises from 6.4% to
18.0%, General E-Commerce Knowledge &amp; QA from 24.7% to 31.4%, and Product
Perception &amp; Understanding falls from 37.5% to 23.6%. Within the general
pool, supervision shifts from captioning and text-only data toward dense text
reading and visually grounded reasoning: OCR, Documents, and Charts rises from
13.7% to 23.8% and Multimodal STEM from 2.9% to 19.0%, while Multimodal
Understanding falls from 26.4% to 8.1% and Pure Text from 26.7% to 19.2%.
Throughout CPT, we track per-domain validation losses to guide mixture adjustments.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training schedule and objective.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All model sizes follow the same two-stage CPT schedule: Stage 1 trains on 370.3B tokens at a 16K sequence length, and Stage 2 extends the context window to 32K for 76.7B tokens. For a training batch <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the visual inputs of example <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> its token sequence, and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> its supervised response token positions with <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{i}=|\mathcal{M}_{i}|&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{i}=|\mathcal{M}_{i}|&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. To prevent long responses from dominating gradient updates while still accounting for sequence length, we employ square averaging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">86</a>]</cite>, weighting each supervised token by <math id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="N_{i}^{-1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{i}^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CPT}}(\theta;\mathcal{B})=-\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}N_{i}^{-1/2}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{M}_{i}}\log\pi_{\theta}(z_{i,t}\mid v_{i},z_{i,&lt;t})}{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}\sqrt{N_{i}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>CPT</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow></msub><mi>N</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mi>log</mi><mi>π</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>v</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow></msub><msqrt><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CPT}}(\theta;\mathcal{B})=-\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}N_{i}^{-1/2}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{M}_{i}}\log\pi_{\theta}(z_{i,t}\mid v_{i},z_{i,&lt;t})}{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}\sqrt{N_{i}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We train with dynamic micro-batching, visual-encoder parallelism, and sequence packing up to each stage’s context limit, preserving per-example loss masks and image–text alignments.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Post-Training</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following CPT, our post-training pipeline combines OPD, parameter-space model merging, and GRPO-based reinforcement learning. Both post-training stages optimize a single set of weights to support both thinking and non-thinking modes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">99</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.2.1 </span>Post-Training Data</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The post-training corpus spans general reasoning, visual perception, and instruction following alongside core e-commerce workflows such as variant matching and product detection. All model sizes share a curated pool of 499,998 OPD prompts—including specialist data for open-vocabulary detection, complex counting, and long-document QA—and 30,976 prompts for RL. We select OPD prompts via offline teacher–student comparisons, retaining instances where the teacher achieves a higher mean quality score than the student. For RL, we sample multiple rollouts from the corresponding post-OPD merged checkpoint and retain prompts with positive reward variance while filtering out already saturated instances (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2" title="Post-training prompt screening. ‣ A.1 Post-Training Hyperparameters and Prompt Curation ‣ Appendix A Training and Data Details ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.2.2 </span>Hybrid Thinking</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To support both deliberative chain-of-thought reasoning (thinking mode) and low-latency direct responses (non-thinking mode) within a single checkpoint, both OPD and RL assign training prompts to thinking and non-thinking modes at a <math id="S2.SS2.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4{:}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4{:}1</annotation></semantics></math> ratio (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3" title="Mode assignment. ‣ A.1 Post-Training Hyperparameters and Prompt Curation ‣ Appendix A Training and Data Details ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>). Because per-response loss averaging assigns lower per-token weight to final answer tokens in longer reasoning traces, allocating a higher proportion of prompts to thinking mode balances supervision across both paradigms. During RL, all rollouts within a prompt group share the same operating mode.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.2.3 </span>On-Policy Distillation</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OPD provides dense, token-level teacher supervision on trajectories sampled from the student policy <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>. We use a post-trained WeMM-Ecom-9B teacher for the 0.8B and 2B models, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B for the 4B model, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B for the 9B and 35B-A3B models. Given a student-generated prefix <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i,t}=(x_{i},y_{i,&lt;t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i,t}=(x_{i},y_{i,&lt;t})</annotation></semantics></math> of response <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, the teacher evaluates the token <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i,t}</annotation></semantics></math> sampled by the rollout policy <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding a token-level distillation signal applied identically in both modes:</p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}}=\log\pi_{T}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})-\log\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>KD</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}}=\log\pi_{T}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})-\log\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the teacher policy. At any fixed prefix, the expected negative signal corresponds to the reverse KL divergence from <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. Holding <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>KD</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}}</annotation></semantics></math> fixed during gradient updates and letting <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{i,t}=\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})/\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{i,t}=\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})/\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the importance ratio, we minimize the clipped actor objective over batch <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> and scored token positions <math id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S2.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPD}}(\theta)=-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}_{i}|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{R}_{i}}\min\!\bigl(\rho_{i,t}a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}},\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,t},0.8,1.2)a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}}\bigr)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>OPD</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mpadded style="width:1.653em;" width="1.653em"><mi>min</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>KD</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>clip</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>KD</mi></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{OPD}}(\theta)=-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}_{i}|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{R}_{i}}\min\!\bigl(\rho_{i,t}a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}},\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,t},0.8,1.2)a_{i,t}^{\mathrm{KD}}\bigr).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">To combine domain adaptation with the broad instruction-following priors of the backbone, we merge once after OPD and before RL by interpolating the vision and language parameters of the OPD checkpoint with the corresponding post-trained Qwen3.5 checkpoint using equal weights <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">2.2.4 </span>Reinforcement Learning</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further refine the models via GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">74</a>]</cite> using task-specific verifiable rewards. For a prompt <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> from task family <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, we sample <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> responses and compute scalar rewards <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{i}=R_{\tau}(x,y_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{i}=R_{\tau}(x,y_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, normalizing advantages across the group:</p>
<table id="S2.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{A}_{i}=\frac{r_{i}-\bar{r}}{\operatorname{std}(r_{1},\ldots,r_{G})+\epsilon_{A}},\qquad\bar{r}=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i}r_{i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>std</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>G</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></munder><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{A}_{i}=\frac{r_{i}-\bar{r}}{\operatorname{std}(r_{1},\ldots,r_{G})+\epsilon_{A}},\qquad\bar{r}=\frac{1}{G}\sum_{i}r_{i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Task rewards check predicted equivalence labels for product matching, score visual grounding and detection by weighted box IoU, and measure constraint satisfaction for instruction following (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" title="E-commerce and general task rewards. ‣ A.2 Reward Design and RL Optimization ‣ Appendix A Training and Data Details ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>). With <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{i,t}=\log\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{i,t}=\log\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})</annotation></semantics></math> and a frozen reference policy initialized from the pre-RL checkpoint, each online rollout batch <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> minimizes</p>
<table id="S2.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{RL}}(\theta)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{B}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}}\frac{1}{|\mathcal{R}_{i}|}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{R}_{i}}\left[-\widehat{A}_{i}\exp\!\big(\ell_{i,t}-\operatorname{sg}(\ell_{i,t})\big)+0.01K_{i,t}\right]," stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.370em;" width="1.370em"><mi>exp</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>0.01</mn><mo lspace="0em" <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>sg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the stop-gradient operator and <math id="S2.SS2.SSS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{i,t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{i,t}</annotation></semantics></math> penalizes KL divergence from the reference policy (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Reward Design and RL Optimization ‣ Appendix A Training and Data Details ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Training Configuration</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CPT employs hybrid AdamW–Muon optimization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>, <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>, combining AdamW updates with Muon’s orthogonalized momentum. Table <a href="#S2.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 2.3 Training Configuration ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarizes the training hyperparameters across all four stages for WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B. At the 9B scale, CPT uses a peak learning rate of <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> and a global batch size of 2,048 sequences. Across all five model sizes, OPD and RL use a constant learning rate of <math id="S2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math> and a global batch size of 2,048 sampled responses.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>E-Commerce Evaluation Framework</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Evaluating multimodal models for real-world commerce requires testing whether they can interpret complex product listings, align variants across views, enforce platform governance rules, and localize advertised items in livestream frames. We construct a comprehensive evaluation suite of 28 benchmarks—comprising 23 in-house benchmarks and five public benchmarks, totaling 207,117 evaluation instances—organized into the eight core scenarios illustrated in Figure <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 3 E-Commerce Evaluation Framework ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. Because the in-house benchmarks derive from proprietary business data, we detail their task definitions, input modalities, and scoring metrics in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Evaluation Benchmarks and Protocols ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To prevent data contamination between training and business evaluation splits, we enforce strict deduplication across splits using product identifiers, cryptographic hashes for exact image duplicates, perceptual hashes for near duplicates, and visual embedding similarity.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.30662v1/commerce_scenarios.svg" id="S3.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:448/199;" width="448" height="199"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S3.F4.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Overview of the eight e-commerce evaluation scenarios.<span id="S3.F4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Seven in-house scenarios are organized around an illustrative product listing into evidence extraction, product interpretation, and decision making, with representative prompts and target outputs (green), complemented by five public benchmarks in E-commerce (Open). Numbers in gray denote instance counts.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evidence extraction (Product OCR and Product Grounding).</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Product OCR (19,962 instances) evaluates fine-grained text recognition and specification reading across single product photos, multi-angle gallery views, and long promotional strips. Product Grounding (six benchmarks, 11,939 instances) assesses spatial localization of target products (Product Detection), brand logos (Logo Detection), certification marks (Qualification Detection), specification tables (Chart Detection), dimension annotations (Dimension Detection), and advertised items in livestream frames (Livestream Detection, 1,992 instances).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Product interpretation (Product Knowledge, Product Attributes, and Product Retrieval).</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Product Knowledge (two benchmarks, 4,598 instances) tests fine-grained entity recognition and domain knowledge across products, brands, and industry standards. Product Attributes (four benchmarks, 26,676 instances) evaluates attribute value extraction, brand attribution, and multi-choice property selection from interleaved images and structured fields. Product Retrieval (three benchmarks, 21,584 instances) benchmarks cross-item matching at three granularity levels: judging visual similarity between cropped regions (Region-level), determining whether two multimodal listings represent the same product (Product-level), and verifying exact variant equivalence from SKU specifications (SKU-level).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decision making (Product Moderation and E-commerce Reasoning).</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Product Moderation (three benchmarks, 6,443 instances) evaluates rule-grounded compliance decisions, including detecting prohibited goods, enforcing category sales restrictions, and identifying image–title mismatches. E-commerce Reasoning (four benchmarks, 3,500 instances) comprises single-image analytical tasks covering chart reasoning, taxonomy classification, constrained product counting, and spatial relation reasoning, where reference answers are programmatically derived from the underlying product tables and query constraints.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Public benchmark coverage.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The E-commerce (Open) scenario incorporates 112,415 instances from five public benchmarks: ShoppingMMLU and ChineseEcomQA for e-commerce concepts and operations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>, <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>, RAIR for rule-aware search relevance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>]</cite>, and EcomMMMU and IndustryBench-MIPU for multimodal product understanding and multi-image industrial attribute extraction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Results</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate all five WeMM-Ecom models in both thinking and non-thinking modes, using a single shared checkpoint per model scale across both operating modes and across both evaluation suites. Our primary comparison pairs each WeMM-Ecom model with the corresponding post-trained Qwen3.5 baseline of the same parameter scale and mode across all 28 e-commerce benchmarks and 64 general-purpose benchmarks.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation protocol.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report the unweighted mean of primary metrics across the 28 e-commerce benchmarks and, separately, across the 64 general benchmarks on a 0–100 scale (where RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg are averaged into a single RefCOCO score and the English and Chinese splits of MMBench count as separate benchmarks). Tasks requiring open-ended semantic adjudication use Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib95" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>]</cite> as an independent judge, distinct from the Qwen3.5-122B-A10B verifier used during RL training. In flagship comparisons, each external baseline is reported under its best-performing evaluated operating mode, i.e., whichever of thinking and non-thinking mode scores higher for that model. Detailed scoring protocols and decoding settings are provided in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Evaluation Benchmarks and Protocols ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>E-Commerce Results</h3>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Flagship comparison.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Dense models. ‣ 4.2 E-Commerce Results ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> compares WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B against leading open-source flagships, including Qwen3.8-Flash-Next <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">66</a>]</cite>, HY4 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">80</a>]</cite>, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">65</a>]</cite>, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, and GLM-5.3-Flash <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib103" title="" class="ltx_ref">103</a>]</cite>. Despite having <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="22\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer total parameters, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B achieves the highest overall average of 74.4 in non-thinking mode, outperforming the strongest baseline, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (73.2), by about 1.2 points.
Substantial gains in Product Retrieval and Product Grounding drive this overall lead (Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Dense models. ‣ 4.2 E-Commerce Results ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>), which remains consistent under alternative scenario weighting schemes.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dense models.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Dense models. ‣ 4.2 E-Commerce Results ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> reports thinking and non-thinking results for all four dense WeMM-Ecom models alongside Qwen3.5-9B and the e-commerce specialist Valley3-32B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>. WeMM-Ecom-9B achieves overall means of 72.5/72.1 (thinking/non-thinking), surpassing Qwen3.5-9B (67.3/65.7) by 5.2/6.4 points, Valley3-32B (64.6/68.6) by 7.9/3.5 points, and the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger Qwen3.8-27B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">68</a>]</cite> (71.8; Figure <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) by 0.7 points. At the compact scales, WeMM-Ecom-4B, 2B, and 0.8B reach 68.7/68.7, 64.2/63.3, and 57.6/56.7, respectively. Across all five model sizes and both operating modes, WeMM-Ecom consistently outperforms size-matched Qwen3.5, with the largest non-thinking improvements reaching +15.5 and +12.3 points at 0.8B and 2B.</p>
</div>
