</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Analysis of E-Commerce Gains</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fine-grained visual localization and cross-listing variant matching account for the largest capability leaps on the e-commerce suite. At the 9B scale, WeMM-Ecom improves upon Qwen3.5-9B across all eight scenario means in thinking mode and seven of eight in non-thinking mode. Product Grounding improves by 15.7 points in thinking mode and 10.3 points in non-thinking mode, while Product Retrieval gains 13.4 points in non-thinking mode—directly reflecting the bounding-box localization and multi-level equivalence supervision introduced in Section <a href="#S2.SS1.SSS1" title="2.1.1 E-Commerce Data ‣ 2.1 Continued Pre-Training for E-Commerce ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Broad improvements beyond grounding.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To confirm that WeMM-Ecom’s advantage extends well beyond spatial localization, we re-evaluate the suite under alternative subsets and weighting schemes.
Excluding all six Product Grounding benchmarks retains clear positive gains over size-matched Qwen3.5 across all ten size–mode pairs—including non-thinking improvements of +11.1 and +8.7 points at 0.8B and 2B—and leaves WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B with the highest mean among the models in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Dense models. ‣ 4.2 E-Commerce Results ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> (75.7 for WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B versus 75.5 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, 75.6 for HY4, and 73.9 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, keeping each model in its Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Dense models. ‣ 4.2 E-Commerce Results ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> operating mode).
Likewise, WeMM-Ecom maintains positive gains across all ten size–mode comparisons when weighting all eight scenarios equally (+2.1 to +14.8 points, which also preserves the flagship ranking), when omitting any single scenario (at least +0.9 points), or when excluding the two probability-readout retrieval sets (+3.1 to +17.8 points).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scenario-level trade-offs and format robustness.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While overall e-commerce performance improves across scales, gains vary by task family: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B is slightly higher on Product Moderation in thinking mode, and Qwen3.5-9B slightly leads WeMM-Ecom-9B on E-commerce Reasoning in non-thinking mode. For structured localization tasks such as Chart Detection, our evaluation parser accepts class predictions under both <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">category</span> and <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">label</span> keys so that comparisons measure localization quality rather than JSON key conventions (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" title="Grounding evaluation protocol. ‣ Appendix B Evaluation Benchmarks and Protocols ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>). Even under this schema-compatible parser, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B outperforms Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on Chart Detection by 8.1 points in thinking mode and 13.0 points in non-thinking mode.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>General Benchmarks</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To assess general-purpose perception and reasoning, we evaluate models across 64 public benchmarks comprising 54 multimodal benchmarks—such as MMBench, MMMU, and MathVista <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>, <a href="#bib.bib101" title="" class="ltx_ref">101</a>, <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>—and 10 text-only benchmarks, including MMLU-Pro and IFEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib87" title="" class="ltx_ref">87</a>, <a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">108</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Comparison with state-of-the-art models.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ Comparison with state-of-the-art models. ‣ 4.4 General Benchmarks ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> compares WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>]</cite>, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>, MiniCPM-V-4.7-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">99</a>]</cite>, and Gemma4-26B-A4B-it <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">78</a>]</cite>. In thinking mode, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B achieves the highest overall average of 76.4, edging out both Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (76.2) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (76.3). In the corresponding non-thinking comparison, WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B scores 72.6, outperforming Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (71.0) by 1.6 points.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Dense models.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Robustness against published baselines. ‣ 4.4 General Benchmarks ‣ 4 Results ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> presents thinking and non-thinking results for our four dense models alongside Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-4.6V-Flash <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>. WeMM-Ecom-9B averages 74.2/69.7 (thinking/non-thinking), outperforming Qwen3.5-9B (73.4/67.6) by 0.8/2.1 points and GLM-4.6V-Flash (63.3/57.9) by 10.8/11.8 points. At the compact scales (4B, 2B, and 0.8B), WeMM-Ecom surpasses size-matched Qwen3.5 in thinking mode by 0.4, 4.5, and 6.9 points, respectively. As shown in Figure <a href="#S0.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, WeMM-Ecom-2B ranks first among lightweight models in non-thinking mode.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Robustness against published baselines.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As a stringent external check, we also compare WeMM-Ecom against an upper-bound Qwen3.5 baseline constructed by taking the higher of our local evaluation and the official Qwen3.5 model-card score <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">69</a>]</cite> on every comparable benchmark. Even against these composite upper bounds (46.2/44.2 at 0.8B and 59.9/55.7 at 2B in thinking/non-thinking modes), WeMM-Ecom-0.8B and WeMM-Ecom-2B maintain substantial overall leads of +6.1/+3.8 and +3.6/+4.7 points, respectively, demonstrating that domain-grounded training and distillation significantly enhance general capabilities in compact models.</p>
</div>

<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented WeMM-Ecom, a family of five multimodal large language models ranging from a dense 0.8B model to a 35B-A3B mixture-of-experts model, together with a 28-benchmark e-commerce evaluation suite that spans eight business scenarios and 207,117 instances. Each model is trained with two stages of continued pre-training that raise the e-commerce share from 45.8% to 61.1%, and then post-trained with hybrid-thinking on-policy distillation, a single parameter-space merge with the post-trained Qwen3.5 backbone, and GRPO, yielding one checkpoint that serves both thinking and non-thinking modes. Across all ten size–mode comparisons, WeMM-Ecom improves on its Qwen3.5 baseline matched to size in e-commerce while matching or surpassing it on average across the 64 general benchmarks. We also show that WeMM-Ecom-35B-A3B attains the highest e-commerce average among evaluated open-source flagships with <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="22\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>22</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">22\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer total parameters, and WeMM-Ecom-9B surpasses the <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger Qwen3.8-27B. This indicates that domain specialization does not necessarily come at the expense of general capabilities, and scale does not gate the specialization benefit.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We release all model weights together with our data curation, training recipe, and benchmark construction so that this recipe can be examined and extended in future endeavors regarding domain-specialized models. In production, WeMM-Ecom already serves hundreds of workflows in WeChat E-Commerce, handling billion-scale requests per day across catalog management, multimodal product search, and livestream commerce. Future work will extend WeMM-Ecom to interactive shopping agents and study hardware-aware quantization for real-time edge deployment.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Training and Data Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Post-Training Hyperparameters and Prompt Curation</h3>

<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Distillation and RL sampling.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">During OPD, we sample two responses per prompt at temperature 1.0 and top-<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> 1.0, with a maximum generation length of 24,576 tokens within a 32,768-token sequence limit. The distillation loss weight is set to 1.0 without an additional reference-policy penalty; compact students (0.8B, 2B, and 4B) initialize from their CPT checkpoints with zero weight decay. During RL, we sample <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=16</annotation></semantics></math> responses per prompt within a 65,536-token context limit using weight decay 0.01, temperature 1.0, and top-<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> 0.9 by default (supplemented with top-<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> 20 and repetition penalty 1.05 on instruction-following tasks). All RL runs initialize both the actor and frozen reference policy from the equally weighted (<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.5</annotation></semantics></math>) post-OPD merged checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Post-training prompt screening.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To construct the OPD prompt pool, both the teacher and student models generate eight candidate responses per prompt; we retain prompts where the teacher achieves a strictly higher mean quality score than the student. For the RL pool, the corresponding post-OPD merged model generates eight thinking-mode rollouts per candidate prompt. We retain prompts with positive reward variance and a mean task reward of at most 0.95, and additionally require a strictly positive mean reward on mathematical and logical reasoning tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mode assignment.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Operating modes are assigned deterministically by hashing each prompt identifier so that all rollouts for a given prompt share the same mode. Thinking mode accounts for 400,229 prompts (80.05%) in the 499,998-prompt OPD pool and 24,823 prompts (80.14%) in the 30,976-prompt RL pool.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Reward Design and RL Optimization</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Equation <a href="#S2.E4" title="Equation 4 ‣ 2.2.4 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 2.2 Post-Training ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, group standard deviations are computed using Bessel’s correction with stabilizer <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{A}=10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{A}=10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> (groups with identical rewards receive zero advantage). In Equation <a href="#S2.E5" title="Equation 5 ‣ 2.2.4 Reinforcement Learning ‣ 2.2 Post-Training ‣ 2 Training ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, the token-level KL penalty is computed via the Schulman approximator <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{i,t}=\min\!\big(10,\exp(d_{i,t})-d_{i,t}-1\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.653em;" width="1.653em"><mi>min</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{i,t}=\min\!\big(10,\exp(d_{i,t})-d_{i,t}-1\big)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i,t}=\operatorname{clip}\!\big(\log\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})-\ell_{i,t},-20,20\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.428em;" width="1.428em"><mi>clip</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>20</mn><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i,t}=\operatorname{clip}\!\big(\log\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y_{i,t}\mid h_{i,t})-\ell_{i,t},-20,20\big)</annotation></semantics></math> and KL coefficient 0.01.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">E-commerce and general task rewards.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Task rewards combine deterministic rule verifiers with model-based judgments from Qwen3.5-122B-A10B. Product and SKU retrieval tasks assign unit reward for predicting the correct equivalence label in the required schema. For localization and detection tasks, let <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> denote the total number of predicted and ground-truth boxes and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the optimal one-to-one matching within each image. For <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, the detection reward is</p>
<table id="A1.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{det}}=\frac{2}{N}\sum_{(p,g)\in\mathcal{P}}\operatorname{IoU}(p,g)\,w(p,g)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>det</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>IoU</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{det}}=\frac{2}{N}\sum_{(p,g)\in\mathcal{P}}\operatorname{IoU}(p,g)\,w(p,g),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(p,g)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(p,g)=1</annotation></semantics></math> for livestream and multi-image detection, and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(p,g)=0.7+0.3\,s(p,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.7</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(p,g)=0.7+0.3\,s(p,g)</annotation></semantics></math> for target-product detection (<math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=1</annotation></semantics></math> for exact class match, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.5</annotation></semantics></math> for partial/full product class confusion, and <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise). For instruction-following tasks, full constraint satisfaction receives reward 1.0, while partial compliance receives <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.49</annotation></semantics></math> times the mean constraint satisfaction score evaluated on the visible final answer after stripping the reasoning block.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Format validation.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Rollouts that violate the required output schema or hit the generation cap before completion receive zero task reward; in thinking mode, responses must contain a well-formed reasoning block followed by a non-empty final answer. If verifier evaluation fails on a prompt group, the task-reward term is masked out and only the reference KL penalty is applied.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Evaluation Benchmarks and Protocols</h2>

<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding and semantic adjudication.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For WeMM-Ecom, thinking mode uses temperature 1.0, top-<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> 0.95, and top-<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> 20, paired with presence penalty 2.0 and repetition penalty 1.05 on reasoning-intensive benchmarks and presence penalty 1.5 with repetition penalty 1.0 on the remaining tasks. In non-thinking mode, standard benchmarks use temperature 0.7 and top-<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> 0.8, while open-ended generation subsets use temperature 1.0, top-<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> 1.0, and top-<math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> 40. All models use a default maximum generation limit of 65,536 tokens (with greedy decoding at 32,768 tokens for OmniDocBench). Baseline models are evaluated under their recommended or task-calibrated decoding parameters. Model-based evaluation adjudication uses Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib95" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>

<span id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Each instance may contain several images, targets, or products.</span></span>

<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Benchmark construction and answer adjudication.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Decoding and semantic adjudication. ‣ Appendix B Evaluation Benchmarks and Protocols ‣ WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> summarizes the 28 e-commerce benchmarks. Product OCR averages accuracies equally across single-image (4,970 instances), multi-image (6,494), and long-image (8,498) subsets. Chart Reasoning averages four 500-question subsets covering SKU charts, price tables, attribute tables, and constraint tables; questions are synthesized under category-specific templates with programmatically computed reference answers and cross-checked by frontier LLMs for reasoning consistency. During evaluation, rule-based matchers first check typed answers and taxonomy aliases before invoking the LLM judge for semantic equivalence. Entity Recognition credits full or partial identifications, Brand tasks allow semantic alias matching, and Image-Title Mismatch requires exact set agreement.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Grounding evaluation protocol.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All six grounding benchmarks use an IoU threshold of 0.5 with coordinates normalized to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1000]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1000</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1000]</annotation></semantics></math>. Chart Detection and Qualification Detection report macro-averaged class F1, whereas the remaining sets report box F1 (with Product Detection using greedy one-to-one matching). In Chart Detection, prompts request JSON objects with <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bbox_2d</span> and <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">category</span>; to ensure schema compatibility across model families, the evaluation parser also accepts class labels output under the <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">label</span> key when <span id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">category</span> is absent.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Retrieval and public benchmark protocols.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Region-level Retrieval, Spearman rank correlation <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> is linearly rescaled to <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50(\rho+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50(\rho+1)</annotation></semantics></math>; for Region-level and Product-level Retrieval, non-thinking mode scores token probabilities whereas thinking mode parses generated labels. Among the public benchmarks, EcomMMMU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> is evaluated on its labeled general test set (GTS) using the main product image and reported as the unweighted mean across its eight subtasks, while IndustryBench-MIPU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">63</a>]</cite> uses multi-image product inputs and reports attribute-extraction micro F1.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

    <a href="https://math.nist.gov/~BMiller/LaTeXML/" target="_blank" class="ltx_ref ltx_LaTeXML_logo">
      <span style="letter-spacing: -0.2em; margin-right: 0.1em;">
        L
        <span style="font-size: 70%; position: relative; bottom: 2.2pt;">A</span>
        T
        <span style="position: relative; bottom: -0.4ex;">E</span>
      </span>
      <span class="ltx_font_smallcaps">xml</span>
      <img alt="[LOGO]"
        src="data:image/png;base64,">
    </a>.
  </div>
  <div class="keyboard-glossary">
    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
